short_name: SDWA sec. 1433 Community Water System Risk & Resilience Assessment and Emergency Response Plan (AWIA 2018 sec. 2013)
summary: Assess risks from malevolent acts and natural hazards incl. resilience of 'electronic, computer, or other automated systems (including the security of such systems)', certify to EPA, review every 5 years, and prepare/certify an ERP within 6 months.
size_thresholds: > 3,300 population served. RRA certification tiers: >= 100,000 (Mar. 31, 2020 / Mar. 31, 2025); 50,000-99,999 (Dec. 31, 2020 / Dec. 31, 2025); 3,301-49,999 (Jun. 30, 2021 / Jun. 30, 2026). ERP certification 6 months later (Sep. 30, 2025; Jun. 30, 2026; Dec. 31, 2026). Wastewater (POTWs) not covered.
status: In effect; second 5-year cycle underway (final ERP deadline Dec. 31, 2026 for smallest tier).

short_name: CIRCIA (Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act of 2022) - proposed 6 CFR Part 226
citation: 6 U.S.C. 681-681g; proposed 6 CFR Part 226 (NPRM 89 FR 23644, Apr. 4, 2024)
summary: Would require covered entities to report covered cyber incidents to CISA within 72 hours and ransom payments within 24 hours, and preserve related data.
applies_to: Entities in a critical infrastructure sector that exceed the SBA small-business size standard for their NAICS code, or meet a sector-based criterion. Sector criterion: owns/operates a community water system or publicly owned treatment works serving > 3,300 people.
size_thresholds: Proposed 226.2(a): exceeds SBA size standard in 13 CFR Part 121 for the entity's NAICS code (employee- or revenue-based depending on NAICS); sector-based criteria apply regardless of size.
status: NOT YET IN EFFECT. NPRM published Apr. 4, 2024; comment period closed Jul. 3, 2024; CISA held additional town halls in 2026 (FR notices Feb. 13, 2026 and May 26, 2026) on scope and burden. Fall 2025 Unified Agenda projected the final rule for 09/2026; no final rule found in the Federal Register as of 2026-09-25. Reporting obligations begin only on the final rule's effective date.
